claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can exist as a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution after solution treatment.
The solution-treated starting material has a low initial dislocation density.
The low hardness and strength of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi are caused by its homogeneous, single-phase solid-solution state.
The homogeneous single-phase structure permits rapid dislocation glide during deformation.
The homogeneous single-phase structure promotes dynamic recovery, including cross-slip, during deformation.
Dynamic recovery limits dislocation accumulation and pile-up.
Limited dislocation accumulation suppresses work hardening and maintains low hardness and yield strength.
At room temperature, the alloy will exhibit relatively low yield strength and hardness.
At room temperature, the alloy will exhibit steady plastic flow.
Cryogenic deformation suppresses dynamic recovery relative to room-temperature deformation.
Suppressing dynamic recovery at cryogenic temperature increases dislocation accumulation and pile-up.
Cryogenically deformed samples will have higher yield strength than comparably deformed room-temperature samples.
Cryogenically deformed samples will have higher hardness than comparably deformed room-temperature samples.
Composition deviations that produce secondary phases may change the proposed recovery behavior.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to homogeneous, single-phase, equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi under room-temperature or cryogenic quasi-static loading.
